## Metadata
Title: FUN'S Cross-Word Puzzles
Author: Harry Cleaver
Copyright: New York World
Date: 1914-03-15
Number: 13
Description: Two puzzles in one: a 13-wide main diamond whose centre is a small inner diamond (r5c7; r6c6-8; r7c5-9; r8c6-8; r9c7), ruled off by a double line, holding an eight-rayed star of three-letter words that all start or end in the printed centre letter E. The four diagonal rays (CUE, RUE, EEN, ELM) print their middle letters (U, U, E, L) on the corners between squares, so those four letters have no square in this grid; the clue answers carry them. Read round from 37 to 44, the ray ends spell AMERICAN. Inside clues are given by end-square pairs such as "E to 37" and "40 to E". The inner star is left out of the grid: its diamond (r5c7; r6c6-8; r7c5-9; r8c6-8; r9c7) is shown as _. Its eight three-letter words, each starting or ending in the printed centre E, are, as printed: E-37. Series of years. (ERA); E-38. A tree. (ELM); E-39. Adam's mate. (EVE); 40-E. To be sorry for. (RUE); 41-E. Frozen water. (ICE); 42-E. Used to billiards. (CUE); 43-E. Used for chopping. (AXE); E-44. A contraction of even. (EEN). 42-E is printed "Used to billiards." for "Used in billiards."
Incomplete: the inner star (eight words around a printed centre E, four of them with a middle letter printed on a corner between squares) can't be represented in an xd grid; its words are in Description.
Source: Milwaukee Sentinel, 1914-03-15, p. 85
Solution-Source: Milwaukee Sentinel, 1914-03-22, p. 85
Numbering: as-printed
